tasks.title: PART I: Use the provided celestial object pointer
tasks.statement: Use the provided celestial object pointer to point at the targets specified in the questions.

parts.question: Move the pointer along the celestial equator.
parts.reference: Evaluated by marker at the observation station.

parts.question: Aim the pointer at the vernal equinox.
parts.reference: Evaluated by marker at the observation station.

parts.question: In the constellation of Pegasus and its vicinity there is an obvious square of bright stars (Great Square of Pegasus), aim the pointer at the brightest star of the square.
parts.reference: Evaluated by marker at the observation station.

parts.question: Aim the pointer at the star named alpha-Arietis (α-Ari).
parts.reference: Evaluated by marker at the observation station.

parts.question: Start from the star named Aldebaran (α-Tauri) in the constellation Taurus, turn the pointer 35 degrees northward followed by 6 degrees westward (in equatorial coordinate). Then, aim the pointer at the brightest star in the field of view.
parts.reference: Evaluated by marker at the observation station.

tasks.title: PART II: Use the provided binoculars
tasks.statement: Use the provided binoculars to observe the objects and then answer the questions by writing or drawing directly in the question sheets.

parts.question: The open star cluster “Hyades” in constellation Taurus is one of the nearest clusters to us, being only 151 light years away. From the provided chart with brightness of some stars indicated by the apparent magnitude in parentheses, please estimate the apparent magnitude of the star Gamma-Tauri (γ-Tauri) to the nearest first decimal digit.
parts.reference: The correct value of brightness of γ-Tauri = 3.6. If the answer is 3.5, 3.6 or 3.7 (5 points). If the answer is 3.3, 3.4, 3.8 or 3.9 (3 points). If the answer is none of the above (0 point).

parts.question: Observe the Andromeda Galaxy (M31) then draw the approximate shape and size of the galaxy that you see through the binoculars in the frame below with correct orientation (in equatorial coordinates). The field of view of the binoculars is 6.8 degrees.
parts.reference: Correct shape and size (between 0.5 to 1 degree) – 3 points. Correct orientation (within 23 degrees of the picture) – 2 points.
